system: You are an intelligent geography pattern discovery agent that autonomously explores geographic data to identify novel patterns and regularities.
region_name: Postfire debris-flow initiation events, southwestern USA (USGS basin-rainstorm event table)

data_description.dataset_name: USGS postfire debris-flow basin-rainstorm event table, Southwest USA (companion data of Fernandez Sirgo et al. 2026, JGR: Earth Surface, DOI 10.1029/2025JF008627)

spatial_coverage.region_name: Burned watersheds in Arizona and New Mexico, USA
spatial_coverage.coverage: Basin-level rainstorm events across ~200 burned watersheds from 14 fires (2010-2021).

data_description.temporal_coverage: Fires ignited 2010-2021; each row is one basin-rainstorm event with a dated storm window and days-since-fire fields.
data_description.spatial_resolution: Basin (watershed) scale; basin lat/lon in the 'Lat and Lon' sheet of data.xlsx
data_description.temporal_unit: Per-event storm timestamps; 'Time since fire start/end (days)' per event
data_description.data_type_numeric: Mixed numeric/categorical; Response is the binary label (1 = debris flow occurred in the basin during the storm, 0 = no response).

table_content.label: Response (2946 no-response vs 161 debris-flow events; 5.2% positive)
table_content.sample_row_note: Rainfall intensities are event peak intensities per duration window; terrain/burn columns are pre-storm basin attributes; soil columns are per-basin properties.

data_description.unit_of_measurement: Rainfall intensity I2-I60: mm/h (nested peak intensities over 2-60 min windows, I2 >= I5 >= ... >= I60 by construction); Cumulative Rain: mm; Duration: minutes; mdNBR/1000: normalized burn-ratio delta (/1000, 0-0.88); MH / L_2_MH / L_3_MH / L_4_MH: burned-area proportions (0-1 / 0-2 scales); Clay / OM / KF: fractions (0-1); Inverse of permeability: 1/K (10.4-87.5); Thickness: m
data_description.data_source: USGS-arizona postfire debris-flow basin-rainstorm event table; companion data published with the paper (GitHub repository attached to the DOI)
data_description.important_note: Structural facts a reader needs before use: (1) the table covers only the FIRST year after fire ignition - 'Time since fire start (days)' spans 22-310 and 'Time since fire end (days)' spans -69..282, so any >=365-day window is empty in this table; 181 events occurred while the fire was still burning (negative days-since-fire-end). (2) Intensity channels are nested peaks, not independent variables. (3) -9999 is the missing-value sentinel (1 cell in 'Number of prior debris-flow-producing storms'); all other listed columns are complete. (4) The soil columns are regional STATSGO texture attributes (identical values for basins sharing a soil polygon); the source publication excluded them from modeling. (5) Debris-flow-positive events exist only for 'Time since fire start' <= 107 days.
data_description.analytical_capabilities: Event-level binary classification and threshold analysis per intensity window; stratification by vegetation type, physiographic province, fire cohort and soil texture; within-first-year temporal stratification (days-since-fire bins). Family data beyond the first year or basin-internal spatial distributions require companion datasets, not this table.
